tools.title: SBSQ #32: SuperMegaJumboDeluxe Edition
tools.summary_raw: It’s three days before the election: the perfect time for an SBSQ reboot.
tools.content_text: The election is on Tuesday, and we’ll publish as much content as we can between now and then. But it’s also Halloween 1 , so let’s have a little fun today. This is the long-awaited (??) revival of Silver Bulletin Subscriber Questions (SBSQ). More specifically, it’s edition #32, which is obviously the Magic Johnson Edition . Most of the questions are election-related, but we’ll take a couple of sports ones at the end. But it’s also the SuperMegaJumboDeluxe Edition. We’re in lightning-round mode here; I’ll give you a couple of relatively off-the-cuff paragraphs on each topic. You can leave questions for SBSQ #33 (the Larry Bird Edition) in the comments below. On the menu today: Why is the Silver Bulletin mascot a wolf? What’s up with the governors’ races in Alaska and Vermont? What if Republicans win the House ? What if the polls froze? Why didn’t 2018’s blue wave reach the Senate? What should we make of big registered vs. likely voter gaps? What can we learn from undecided voters? Does FLIPR account for voter suppression or election interference? The conservative golden age, revisited Should models account for near-misses in sports? Why isn’t there more baseball coverage at Silver Bulletin? Why is the Silver Bulletin mascot a wolf? Sophie asks: Why is the Silver Bulletin mascot a wolf and not a dolphin (for FLIPR)? Officially introducing Sylver. Illustration by Joey Ellis Sylver, who is indeed a wolf 🐺, was recommended by Fivey Fox , and drawn by the same graphic artist as Fivey Fox. I think you’d agree that it would be pretty weird for a fox to be friends with a dolphin? Plus, FLIPR 🐬 can be a slippery fella. The reason we update the forecast only once per day is because we have to go find him in the East River — he’s never quite in the same location — and bribe him with sushi-grade tuna. Fivey, meanwhile, is living out his dreams by having become a ranger at Acadia National Park, where he never has to explain that 30 percent chances are supposed to happen 30 percent of the time. What’s up with the governors’ races in Alaska and Vermont? Jeremy asks: The paid subscribers want to know what is happening with your gubernatorial forecast, specifically with Alaska and Vermont. Those are probably the forecasts where FLIPR is most going out on a limb. What are your feelings about those? V. M. Kozma asks: There is a large gap between FLIPR and prediction markets on the Alaska senate election that completely goes against the overall trend of prediction markets being less positive on Democrats’ chances. An obvious explanation would be that the model fails to handle ranked choice voting. Is there another explanation? Also asked by Mike Shedlock , Trevor , Dan Rader and Kyle . Campaign signs for Mary Peltola and Sen. Dan Sullivan in Anchorage, Oct. 30. (Justin Sullivan/Getty Images) Yeah, these are two highly fascinating races.
